caption: F' (x)=x^3-3*x+a. F has one extremum when a<=-2 or a>=2; -2<a<2 gives three. Among -5,-3,-1,2,4, only a=-1 is in the three-extrema interval, so the answer is ③.

sourceConditions.condition: F' (x)=f(x)=x^3-3*x+a, so F extrema occur exactly where f changes sign.
f' (x)=3*(x-1)*(x+1), with local maximum a+2 at x=-1 and local minimum a-2 at x=1. The one-extremum parameter set is (-infinity,-2] union [2,infinity); the three-extrema set is (-2,2).
Among the five source choices, only a=-1 lies in (-2,2).

newVisualInformation: A parameter number line gives the exact one-extremum and three-extrema regions, then classifies the five source choices against the open three-extrema interval. The point at a=-1 is the only choice inside it; the endpoints a=-2 and a=2 remain included in the one-extremum set.
